references.text: Jesus' prayer for cleansing from sin ("Cleanse me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow!") reflects Jesus' claim that the one who has bathed is clean, even though a simple washing of the feet is required for complete purity.

Jesus' own explanation of the action in verse 10, where he links foot-washing to an example of service and mutual cleansing, expands on the meaning that the disciples are clean but still need this act.
Jesus' statement that the disciples are already clean because of the word he has spoken is a direct theological parallel to the claim in 13:10 that they are clean except for Judas.
John's description of Jesus' blood as cleansing from all sin is the theological basis for the claim that the one who has bathed is completely clean, even though there are exceptions (such as Judas).

The author describes believers' condition as having "hearts cleansed from a guilty conscience" and "bodies washed with pure water," which echoes the distinction between the one who has bathed and the one who still needs further washing.
